# Design Patterns Quest

> A gamified learning platform for mastering all 22 Gang of Four (GoF) design patterns through an RPG adventure with interactive quizzes, XP rewards, and TypeScript code examples.

## Creational Patterns

- [Factory Method](/quest/factory-method): Let subclasses decide which object to create
- [Abstract Factory](/quest/abstract-factory): Create families of related objects without specifying their concrete classes
- [Builder](/quest/builder): Construct complex objects step by step
- [Prototype](/quest/prototype): Clone existing objects without coupling to their classes
- [Singleton](/quest/singleton): Ensure a class has only one instance with a global access point

## Structural Patterns

- [Adapter](/quest/adapter): Make incompatible interfaces work together
- [Bridge](/quest/bridge): Split a large class into two separate hierarchies that can evolve independently
- [Composite](/quest/composite): Compose objects into tree structures and treat them uniformly
- [Decorator](/quest/decorator): Attach new behaviors to objects by wrapping them
- [Facade](/quest/facade): Provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem
- [Flyweight](/quest/flyweight): Share common state between multiple objects to save memory
- [Proxy](/quest/proxy): Provide a substitute that controls access to another object

## Behavioral Patterns

- [Chain of Responsibility](/quest/chain-of-responsibility): Pass requests along a chain of handlers until one handles it
- [Command](/quest/command): Turn requests into stand-alone objects with all request info
- [Iterator](/quest/iterator): Traverse a collection without exposing its internal structure
- [Mediator](/quest/mediator): Reduce chaotic dependencies by centralizing communication
- [Memento](/quest/memento): Save and restore an object's previous state (undo)
- [Observer](/quest/observer): Notify multiple objects about changes in another object
- [State](/quest/state): Let an object change its behavior when its internal state changes
- [Strategy](/quest/strategy): Define a family of interchangeable algorithms
- [Template Method](/quest/template-method): Define the skeleton of an algorithm, letting subclasses fill in steps
- [Visitor](/quest/visitor): Separate algorithms from the objects they operate on

## How It Works

This platform teaches design patterns through gamification:
1. Choose a realm (Creational, Structural, or Behavioral)
2. Complete pattern quests that include explanations, analogies, and TypeScript examples
3. Pass interactive quizzes to earn XP and unlock the next pattern
4. Track progress via the interactive Skill Tree
5. Earn badges and level up as you master more patterns
